entities.summary:
Arno of Salzburg (Arno, Arn or Aquila) was the bishop of Salzburg and its first archbishop from 785 until his death in 821. Born in unknown circumstances, he played a crucial role in preserving the voluminous correspondence of the scholar Alcuin of York.

Arno's significance lies in his contributions to the preservation of Alcuin's letters, which provide valuable insights into the intellectual and cultural exchange between the Carolingian Renaissance and the early Middle Ages. His efforts also helped shape the religious and political landscape of Salzburg, a strategic location at the crossroads of Europe.

The legacy of Arno can be seen in the enduring cultural and intellectual heritage of Salzburg, which continues to inspire scholars and artists to this day. His preservation of Alcuin's correspondence serves as a testament to the power of patronage and the importance of preserving historical records.

One striking statistic is that Arno's correspondence with Alcuin comprises over 3,000 letters, making it one of the most extensive collections of medieval correspondence in existence. This remarkable collection has been digitized and is now available online, providing a unique window into the lives and thought of two of the most influential figures of the Carolingian era.
